detail.longDescription: Whenever I try running any Python file through VS Code, the console returns an error saying that the file or directory does not exist, even though I opened it manually using the 'open folder' option. When I run this code (encoder.py): mode_indicator = '0100' char_count_indicator = '' #debe ser de 8 bits unencoded_text = '' #ingresado por el usuario def encode_text_bin(text: str): text_list = list(text) print(text_list) encode_text_bin('aaa') The console looks like this: me@myComputer:~/Desktop/SEMESTER/HW/QR_ENCODER_DECODER$ /usr/bin/python3 '"/home/me/Desktop/SEMESTER/HW/QR_ENCODER_DECODER/encoder.py"' /usr/bin/python3: can't open file '/home/me/Desktop/SEMESTER/HW/QR_ENCODER_DECODER/"/home/me/Desktop/SEMESTER/HW/QR_ENCODER_DECODER/encoder.py"': [Errno 2] No such file or directory The folder in question looks like this: The only way I can run code while avoiding this is by manually choosing the 'run without debugging' option. I haven't changed any VS Code settings. Why does this error occur, and how can I fix it?
